summary: Toggle accessible name is only an example in the ticket: use 'Add to favourites' and 'Remove from favourites' verbatim on every toggle, without the talk title.
Visible marker form is unspecified: show the text 'Favourite' only on favourited talks, separate from the toggle, so the mark does not rely on colour alone.
A state-dependent name plus aria-pressed announces the state twice: keep both because the ticket requires both.
Stored ids matching no talk are ignored on read: loading never rewrites storage, and the next toggle writes only ids that match a talk.
Non-string entries and duplicates in the stored array are not covered by the ticket: drop them on parse, because a duplicate would keep a talk marked after removal.
First load and last removal are unspecified: a missing key means no favourites and writes nothing, and removing the last favourite stores an empty array.
Layer ownership follows the package conventions: parse and serialise in core, controlled toggle and marker in ui, storage adapter, key and state in agenda.
The ticket only names reload, but a talk must be marked wherever it appears: a toggle on one route must show on the other after client-side navigation.
Failures of the storage API itself and sync between tabs are not in the ticket: both stay out of scope, which only covers bad stored values.
The track filter is unrelated to favourites: favourites survive filter changes, do not reorder the schedule, and add no filter by favourite.
An unknown id at /talks/:id keeps the existing 'Talk not found.' message with no toggle.
Gate A approved without review in headless mode
Gate B verdict Split: 22 files, 460 lines, three layers with 5 new exported symbols; proposed three smaller tickets in core, ui and agenda.
